title: The Doubled Signature
statement: The Doubled Signature is the corpus's hermeneutic principle, extending Hamlet's Mill: each precessional age encodes its astronomical signature in iconographic and religious form doubly — in the age's own zodiacal emblem and in a paired counter-form — so that age-attribution of religious iconography can be cross-checked rather than free-associated; the principle is an interpretive instrument at speculative grade, whose value is the constraint it imposes on the corpus's own age-readings.

includes: The principle as the corpus states it: dual encoding per age, providing a two-witness check on iconographic age-attribution
Its lineage: an extension of the Hamlet's Mill encoding thesis (woh-claim-0014), reserved by that record and minted here from its own entry
Its instrumental function: a constraint on the corpus's readings — an attribution that cannot show both signatures is weakened by the corpus's own rule
The Mithraic tauroctony as the corpus's exhibit case for a doubled age-icon, at the entry's stated strength
excludes: Any claim that ancient iconographers held the principle consciously; it is the corpus's instrument, not their doctrine
Free-association rescue: an attribution failing the double check may not be saved by loosening the pairing
Extension beyond iconographic age-attribution into general symbolism
The astronomical layer itself, which is woh-claim-0003's and 0014's

source_references.locator: The encoding thesis this principle extends (metadata_only; the wantlist's standing item)
The canon's cycle symbolism the corpus's age-readings sit within (TBWTT-3:305 family)

alternatives.statement: Two signatures give more matching surface, not less; unless the pairing is fixed in advance per age, the double check loosens rather than constrains.
The principle inherits Hamlet's Mill's method problems; doubling an unsound attribution procedure does not sound it.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0003 or woh-claim-0014 is revised or retired.
The per-age pairings are not fixed in advance in corpus practice, vindicating the flexibility objection.
Inspection of Hamlet's Mill changes what the extension actually extends.
